- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model often underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% buffer to forecast for early bearish turn.  
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish (e.g., -1.00 to 0.00), model often lags; shift forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to reflect sentiment reversal.  
- In high-event periods (≥18 events/30d), model tends to overestimate volatility; cap forecast range within ±3% of recent 7-day moving average to avoid overfitting.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes (e.g., -0.50, -1.00), model often fails to anticipate sharp drops; add 5–10% downward adjustment for next 3–7 days.
